texts.preamble: Shahnoor Ul Islam vs Nasir Khan And Ors on 24 September, 2025 In The Court Of Sh. Harjyot Singh Bhalla District Judge-03, South-West District, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi Cs Dj 819/2018 Shahnoor Ul Islam v. Nasir Khan and Ors Cnr No. Dlsw01-015118-2018 Shahnoor Ul Islam S/o Taro Babu R/o C-267, Tikona Park, Hastsal Road, Uttam Nagar, New Delhi. ............ Plaintiff Vs. 1. Nasir Khan S/o Shahbaz Khan R/o 806, Sheesh Mahal, Azad Market, Old Delhi-110006. 2. Nazim S/o Nasir Khan R/o 806, Sheesh Mahal, Azad Market, Old Delhi-110006. 3. Salman S/o Nasir Khan R/o 806, Sheesh Mahal, Azad Market, Old Delhi-110006. 4. Rajeev Kumar S/o Hari Singh R/o J-32, Vikas Puri, New Delhi.
texts.facts: The present suit has been filed by the plaintiff for relief of possession, permanent injunction and recovery of mesne profits. Shahnoor Ul Islam vs Nasir Khan And Ors on 24 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184241293/ 1 2. The plaintiff was running a registered dhaba under the name and title as "M/s Laziz Zaika India" at Shop no. B-1/1, Ground and First Floor, Gulab Bagh, Nawada, New Delhi (hereinafter referred to as suit property). The said shop was taken by the plaintiff on lease from defendant no.4 for a period of three years i.e. from 01.03.2017 to 28.02.2020 vide registered lease deed executed in favour of plaintiff by its owner. The said business was registered in the name of plaintiff vide registration no. 23317007000059 issued by Department of Food Safety vide certificate dated 27.01.2017. 3. That defendant no.1 approached the plaintiff and requested to give him some work in his dhaba and plaintiff kept the defendant no.1 in the dhaba on monthly basis. That after some time, defendant no.1 had brought his two sons (defendant no.2 and 3) with him in order to work on the dhaba without the knowledge and consent of plaintiff. That the plaintiff objected to the unauthorized activity of the defendant no.1 but defendant no.1 to 3 started threatening the plaintiff with dire consequences. 4. That on 02.06.2017 at about 8:30 PM all the defendants went to the suit property of the plaintiff and shouted there. Thereafter, they all also went to the house of plaintiff and demanded key of the suit property and upon refusal they gave blows to the plaintiff. That the defendants snatched the keys of the suit property from the plaintiff and ran away from there by extending threats to the plaintiff not to come near the suit property or else the family of the plaintiff would be killed by them. That the plaintiff lodged a written complaint at PS Bindapur and copy of the same was given to the Commissioner of Police but no action was taken by the police. 5. Summons were sent to the defendants. None entered appearance on behalf of the defendants. 6. On 16.01.2020, the following order was passed by my Ld. Predecessor and the relevant portion is quoted for ease of reference: Cost Rs.5,000/ imposed upon defendant No. 4 on 27.07.2019 has not been paid till date and proxy counsel requests next date for payment of cost by stating that defendant No. 4 is suffering from viral fever. Order dated 27.07.2019 allowing defendant's application for condoning delay of seven months in filing written statement being conditional order is kept in abeyance and defendant No. 4 is directed to appear in person for examination and payment of cost Rs.5,000/ on next date failing which his written statement will be taken on off record. 7. On 21.01.2020, the following order was passed by my Ld. Predecessor and the relevant portion is quoted for ease of reference: Since conditional order dated 27.07.2019 condoning delay of seven months in filing written statement of defendant No.4 has not been complied so written statement of defendant No.4 is taken off record and he is proceeded ex-parte. 8. Plaintiff examined himself as PW-1. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon the following documents: (a) Site plan as Ex. PW 1/1; (b) Copy of lease agreement marked as Mark A ; (c) Copy of registration certificate as Ex. PW 1/3 (OSR) ; (d) Copy of MLC marked as Mark B ; (e) Copy of police complaint marked as Mark C. 10. 11. The plaintiff was, unfortunately, only a tenant of defendant no.4. The suit is not under Section 6 of CPC. 12. As far as damages are concerned, plaintiff only claims to be a tenant of defendant no.4 and had to prove the loss suffered by him, because of dispossession.
